newsitem.title: UK: Ivorian debt attractive after Brady deal-Paribas.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian debt attractive after Brady deal-Paribas.

text.p: Investors should be overweight in Ivorian debt following this month's agreement with London Club creditors, Paribas Capital Markets said on Friday.
Commercial creditors agreed to reschedule the Ivory Coast's $7.2 billion of debt on November 21.

"The amount of debt forgiveness implied by this agreement -- about 80 percent of principal and PDI (past-due interest) -- has significant and positive implications for the Ivory Coast as a sovereign credit," the bank said in a research report.
It expected the country's Brady bonds to trade between the equivalent Nigerian and and Bulgarian assets in the shorter term.
"In the medium-to-long-term, Ivory Coast Brady debt could trade through Nigerian Bradys on a stripped spread basis," it added.
The stripped spread calculates the value of a Brady bond without its collateral.
In terms of structural reform, the Ivory Coast is far ahead of both the other countries with a more stable economic policy, it said.

It noted that while Bulgaria is currently debating to introduction of a currency board, the Ivory Coast's membership of the CFA franc zone meant it it had effectively used such a system for over 30 years.
Paribas preferred the front-loaded interest reduction bond (FLIBR) option to the discount bond under the London Club deal.
Over time it expected demand for the bonds to considerably outweigh the selling by bank holders of the debt.
"We still maintain our overweight recommendation on Ivory Coast and believe that those investors who lack exposure should buy the loans at current levels," it added.
